mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 3.0% indicates sustained monetary tightening, increasing discount rates for equity cash flows and reducing valuation multiples, which produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point increase in unemployment rate over the prior 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A joint condition of FEDFUNDS above 3.0% and UNRATE above 4.0% indicates monetary tightening combined with labor market weakness, increasing recession risk and reducing equity valuations, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3.0 and UNRATE > 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, housing starts below 1400 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand, reducing retail sales growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1400 during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 295 indicates persistent inflation, forcing the Federal Reserve to maintain high interest rates that increase the cost of capital and reduce equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 295.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 (index) signals a manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate output and profit margins, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts below 1400 thousand units and retail sales below 680,000 million dollars signals broad-based consumer demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1400 and RSAFS < 680000.

mechanism_narrative: In labor market recovery phases, a monthly payroll employment increase exceeding 100 thousand persons signals strong job growth, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which causes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS change > 100 during labor market recovery.
